title: Add error handling and logging to resetFirestoreNetwork's disable/enable sequence in firestore_instance_provider.dart

evidence.quote:
final reset = resetFirestoreNetwork;
      if (reset != null) await reset();

why: resetFirestoreNetwork disables then re-enables the Firestore network with no try/catch and no AppLogger call. If enableNetwork() throws after disableNetwork() succeeds (plugin channel error, terminated instance, or exactly the flaky-network condition this function exists to recover from), the network is left force-disabled with no automatic retry and zero diagnostic trail. The connectivity-trigger caller in sync_orchestrator.dart (line ~611) does wrap this in try/catch+log, but the lifecycle/foreground-resume caller in lifecycle_observer.dart:147-148 does not — an exception there aborts the rest of the resume sequence (redetectTimezone, invalidateSacredCache, triggerPull) as an unhandled async error, silently skipping the resume pull.
recommendation: Wrap the disable/enable pair in try/catch inside resetFirestoreNetwork itself (so every caller gets the protection for free), log failures via AppLogger with a stable event code, and consider a bounded retry for enableNetwork() specifically so a mid-sequence failure doesn't leave the channel permanently disabled.
acceptance_criteria: resetFirestoreNetwork catches and logs failures from disableNetwork()/enableNetwork() instead of letting them propagate unhandled.

Unit test: stub FirebaseFirestore so enableNetwork() throws after disableNetwork() succeeds; assert the exception is caught/logged and does not abort the lifecycle-resume sequence (timezone redetect, sacred-cache invalidation, resume pull still run).

corrections: EH-1 global handlers ARE installed (logger.dart:86-93, crashlytics_bootstrap.dart:26-30), so an escaping exception is NOT 'zero diagnostic trail' — it gets generically logged via AppLogger.handle. The core claim (resume steps silently skipped) still holds; only the diagnostics framing is overstated.
